newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt opposes encryption keys for German police.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt opposes encryption keys for German police.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on Friday said he rejected the idea of letting law enforcement officials have technology that can tap into encrypted phone calls and computer data.

"For several years the economics ministry has prevented such a law from coming," Rexrodt said in a statement. "I spoke out unmistakably against limiting the use of encryption products" at the CeBIT electronics trade fair in March.
Earlier this week Interior Minister Manfred Kanther called for a law requiring makers of encryption technology to provide decoding "keys" to police.
Otherwise, criminals using cellular phones, computers and other high-tech gear have an advantage, said Kanther, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU).

"The criminals are hiding in the anonymity of the networks, wiping their electronic tracks," Kanther said. "The technical and organisational competence of agencies charged with fighting computer crime must be strengthened."
Kanther's statements added fuel to a debate about control of the Internet computer network.
Rexrodt, a member of Kohl's junior coalition partners, the Free Democrats (FDP), said his stance on encryption was being used "for political games".
